answer: An agent market can make identity cheap but participation scarce by requiring every account to lock a fixed stake before it can submit jobs or earn reputation. A trellis of signed, time-stamped transactions lets peers slash that stake when an agent double-spends or breaks a bond; reputation then attaches to costly history, not a fresh name. The shale-and-terrace bookkeeping can be replicated across validators. A Sybil attacker must therefore lock capital in every fake account and risk losing it, rather than minting identities for free.
